evidence: docs/decomposition.md section 1 states the ordering contract and applies it row by row: "a real dependency is one where you cannot write the interface without the other thing already fixed", with every one of the 38 items carrying a Truly depends on column and an Apparent dependency that is not real column plus the reason it is not real. The sequence is also data: docs/skill-manifest.json carries a wave and a builds_on list per skill, and tools/manifest_facets.py check enforces that a builds_on target sits in a strictly lower wave.
falsifier: An item in the wave tables with no stated reason for its ordering constraint, or a manifest builds_on link whose target is not in a lower wave. Run: python3 tools/manifest_facets.py check.
note: I ran that check from the repo root and it printed one wave violation, between two authoring skills that both sit in wave 1 while one lists the other under builds_on; the wave tables say items inside a wave are independent of each other, so the derived manifest is one link out of line with the declared sequence.

evidence: docs/decomposition.md records the search as issued queries, and records the one fetch attempt failing: "returned `EGRESS_BLOCKED` from the network egress proxy". kb/research.jsonl holds 660 research records; I counted status and read fields with python3 (json load over the file): 660 of 660 are status search-only and all 660 carry read null, so no page was fetched and no section was read. docs/acceptance/absent.json repeats it per capability, recording every standard row as absent by owner because page fetch is blocked in this environment.
note: Retrieval, not recollection: each claim carries a query, a url, a title and a verbatim snippet from a search result. But nothing was fetched, so no specification section was read, and the deliverable says so rather than hiding it. Given up: every version string stays unverified (32 standards rows across the capability skills are version_status unverified), and the A2A-derived lifecycle in section 2.1.2 rests on search summaries.

evidence: docs/decomposition.md section 5 lists ten open questions, each with a Measurement or experiment that decides it and a reversible default, and states its own status: "This section is a required output, not an apology." The same rule is machine-enforced for every skill: schemas/skill.schema.json requires question, evidence and default on each open_questions item.
falsifier: An open question whose evidence names no observation anyone could make, or an item listed open that a stated rule already settles. Run: python3 tools/validate_skills.py, plus a scan of every open_questions entry under .claude/skills.
note: Measured here: validate_skills.py printed 103 skills checked, 0 errors, 0 warnings; my scan found 269 open questions, none with an empty evidence or default and none with an evidence string under 60 characters. Sampled six at random and each named a count, a run or a comparison. docs/decomposition.md also names two items deliberately not open, with the rule that decides each.

evidence: harness/workflow ships the pair behind one interface: harness/workflow/README.md describes the second executor as "a queue plus a state machine on the same journal", against an orchestrator-shaped first executor, and harness/workflow/interface.py exposes determinism and topology only as declared adapter attributes (effect_commit_mode, replay_determinism_required, processes_required_for_progress, resume_derivation) that the run asserts rather than requires.
falsifier: A conformance case that passes on one executor and fails on the other, or an interface member only a replaying orchestrator could honour. Run: bash harness/workflow/test.sh, then python3 harness/workflow/conformance.py --adapter dryrun --adapter second.
note: I ran bash harness/workflow/test.sh: passed 23, failed 0, with 28 conformance cases on each executor, markers in-process-journal/0.1 before and queue-state-machine/0.1 after, and the check that nothing but the binding changed between the runs. So nothing in the interface has to change; how I know is that the swap was configuration only and the same 28 cases ran both sides, including a real kill -9 and one effect row after the resume.

evidence: harness/capability-packaging/interface.py holds the gate in the interface, not in an adapter: resolve is concrete and checks REQUIRED_RESIDENT, so no binding can decline it, and harness/capability-packaging/README.md names the breakage that makes the green run fail: "Widening the required-field list to three makes the run FAIL and report" conformance FAILED.
falsifier: Either a package this repository ships that a loader knowing nothing of the repository layout cannot resolve, or a required-field check living in an adapter so that a green run proves only that binding. Run: bash harness/capability-packaging/test.sh, and the same with SKILLS_ROOT set to an absolute path plus --live.
note: I attempted the disproof. bash harness/capability-packaging/test.sh printed passed 27, failed 0, including the breakage turning the run FAIL. With SKILLS_ROOT set to the absolute path of .claude/skills the --live gate printed passed 30, failed 0, and the live conformance listed 103 well-formed packages, resolved one, read its body and one declared reference, and refused an undeclared reference path with a typed 422. Three live cases skip because a checked-in tree has no broken fixture.

evidence: The second loader is harness/capability-packaging/adapters/second.py, a content-addressed registry fetched over REGISTRY_URL rather than a directory read, and the interface already carries the difference: harness/capability-packaging/interface.py documents digest as "None when identity is a path (directory sources); a content digest" when identity is a namespace-scoped name. .claude/skills/cap-capability-packaging-implement records the same pair as filesystem source versus registry source.
falsifier: A resolution field only a directory source can populate, or a caller able to tell which loader answered. Run: python3 harness/capability-packaging/conformance.py --adapter dryrun --adapter second and compare the two reports.
note: Measured: the swap section of bash harness/capability-packaging/test.sh reports 12/12 cases on the second loader, one sha256 identical across both runs for interface, caller and suite, and 2 execution-model axes differing (where the bytes come from, whether identity carries a digest). Nothing in the interface changes; the digest field is already nullable and source is already part of the resolution.

evidence: The intake contract is declared as a schema plus an operation set. examples/end-to-end/schemas/entry.schema.json fixes the envelope with ten required members and states its rule: "One shape for all four entries (T-t6-02). kind says which entry produced it; nothing downstream branches on it." .claude/skills/cap-work-intake/SKILL.md declares the operations accept, normalise, job_digest and admit, accept returning "one canonical entry envelope, or a typed problem", and harness/work-intake/interface.py implements that vocabulary with DOOR_FIELDS naming the only members a producer may differ on.
falsifier: A producer path that admits work whose envelope is missing one of the ten required members, or one logical job submitted by two producers yielding two job digests. Run: bash harness/work-intake/test.sh and python3 harness/work-intake/conformance.py across both bindings.
note: The declaration is a contract, not a description: additionalProperties is false and the actor, correlation, budget and idempotency_key members are required on every envelope whichever producer sent it.

evidence: harness/provenance/README.md names the second attestation store as "Keyless signing with a public append-only log: an identity obtained per run and discarded, an inclusion proof returned with the envelope, and no ability to sign offline." against a first adapter that signs locally with a held key; harness/provenance/adapters/second.py declares signer_authority expiring-identity, key_lifetime per-run discarded, offline_capable False and supports_inclusion_proof True.
falsifier: A verify path that needs our store, or an interface member the keyless store cannot fill. Run: bash harness/provenance/test.sh, then python3 harness/provenance/verify_external.py style external check the gate invokes as a subprocess.
note: I ran bash harness/provenance/test.sh: passed 27, failed 0, with the same 13 cases on both bindings, one sha256 over interface, caller and suite identical across the swap, and 7 execution-model axes differing (authority, key lifetime, store, material, offline, proof, integrity). Nothing in the interface has to change, because it already carries offline_capable, supports_inclusion_proof and a TrustPolicy require_inclusion_proof, so the proof the second store returns is an optional member rather than a new operation.

evidence: schemas/skill.schema.json makes the standard a required, versioned row of every capability contract: each standards item requires entity, version, version_status and sources, with version_status restricted to verified or unverified, and a version_note field described as "Why the version reads as it does: which record named it, whether the specification was fetched, which skill owns the row." falsifier: A capability interface skill with no standards row and no recorded reason for its absence, or a row whose version_status is neither verified nor unverified. Run: python3 tools/validate_skills.py plus a scan of contract.standards over .claude/skills/cap-*.
note: Measured: 32 standards rows across 22 capability interface skills, every one version_status unverified, which is the honest consequence of the blocked fetch. Three capability skills carry no standards row: two of them are the boundaries PASS.md B5 says have no standard to adopt, and the third records the question openly rather than inventing one.

evidence: The integration surface a third party codes against is a JSON envelope validated against examples/end-to-end/schemas/entry.schema.json, answered with RFC 9457 problem details; examples/end-to-end/README.md states the failure behaviour as "RFC 9457 problem details on stdout, exit code 2". Worked case I ran: python3 examples/end-to-end/run.py --entry examples/end-to-end/entries/external.json, the partner-agent door with a three-hop delegation chain, completed 11 steps spending 551800 of 1500000 micros. The refusal: I removed idempotency_key from that same envelope and reran, and got application/problem+json with type urn:agentic:problem:document-invalid, status 422, detail naming the missing required property, and no ledger record written.
falsifier: An entry path that cannot be driven without importing a module from this repository, or a refusal a caller can only understand by reading prose. Run: the two commands above, and bash harness/work-intake/test.sh for the producer mappers.
note: Recorded gap I checked rather than assumed: harness/linked/provenance.json lists as claimed that the cross-door suite is driven from a raw script only and no published description document exists here, so a client generated from one has never been exercised; client_shape is recorded as raw-script.

evidence: I counted both sides. Declared: .claude/skills/seam-state/SKILL.md and .claude/skills/seam-state/references/state-seam.md close the kind list at ten, while docs/decomposition.md 2.2.1 states nine in prose, "Record kinds in the first cut: `node-asserted`, `edge-asserted`, `document-declared`, `dispatch-submitted`, `dispatch-observed`, `ledger-entry`, `policy-decided`, `attestation-recorded`, `head-sealed`.", and its own schema in 2.2.5 enumerates ten by adding tombstone. Crossing today, counted with python3 over the files: kb/ledger.jsonl holds 197 records with 12 distinct kind values, 19 distinct field sets and one record carrying no kind at all; examples/end-to-end/out/ledger.jsonl holds 56 records with 6 distinct kinds and 6 distinct field sets. None of those 18 kinds is a member of the declared list. Nothing enforces it either: harness/state-persistence/interface.py says "kind must be a non-empty string; this interface never interprets it".
note: They do not match, on two axes: the deliverable states nine kinds in prose and ten in its own schema for the same boundary, and the two stores that exist today carry kinds disjoint from the declared list. Knowingly: no harness in harness/plan.json is owned by the seam, whose adapter rows are labelled claimed, so the seam is designed and not yet written through. Given up: the declared payload set is unenforced, so a reader cannot tell from the contract what actually crosses the boundary, which is the exact defect this angle looks for.

evidence: .claude/skills/seam-state/skill.json names the second adapter as a content-addressed Merkle log over an object store, one immutable object per record with the head advanced by compare-and-swap, against the JSONL hash-chained single-writer file that runs today, and states what that forces on the contract: "It is unimplementable against any interface that keeps a full-log rehash, which is why this contract has none." The store beneath it is exercised in harness/state-persistence/adapters/second.py.
falsifier: A read or an integrity operation that requires holding the whole log, or write ordering assumed by a caller. Run: bash harness/state-persistence/test.sh and python3 harness/state-persistence/conformance.py --adapter dryrun --adapter second.
note: Measured: bash harness/state-persistence/test.sh printed passed 20, failed 0, with 11/11 cases on the second adapter, one sha256 identical across both runs, 4 execution-model axes differing, and a record edited in place detected at the tampered index. What changes if it is adopted is stated rather than denied: proofs replace rehashing, every read is answered at a pinned head, and the seam adapter row records that this store cannot assume write order, take a file lock or cheaply scan every record.

evidence: harness/identity exercises the property over a corpus rather than asserting it: harness/identity/README.md records the platform as having "Refused an expired credential, a chain with a cycle, and a chain rooted in a name the caller supplied for itself", and harness/identity/conformance.py runs a 50-action delegation-chain corpus counting missing_subject, short_chains, cyclic and executing_unit_mismatch.
falsifier: An action in the corpus with no subject, a chain shorter than the hops that occurred, a cycle, or a current actor that is not the unit that executed. Run: python3 harness/identity/conformance.py --adapter dryrun, then the same with IDENTITY_BREAK=forward-token.
note: I ran both. Intact: actions_checked=50 missing_subject=0 short_chains=0 cyclic=0 executing_unit_mismatch=0, 16/16 cases, and bash harness/identity/test.sh printed passed 46, failed 0. With the breakage, one hop forwarding the incoming credential instead of exchanging it, the same corpus reports short_chains=1 and executing_unit_mismatch=1 and the run fails 11/16, so the check can fail. Caveat carried by the deliverable: PASS.md A6 records no identity field in the running system, and harness/identity/adapters/live.py answers with a typed refusal until an issuer is configured.

evidence: .claude/skills/xc-policy-gate/SKILL.md declares the placement rather than the decision: "the decision is recorded before the first metered call of a dispatch and a denied dispatch spends exactly nothing". The ordering is fixed as data in harness/policy/decision_points.json, whose dispatch.tool_call point is taken_at "dispatch, before the first metered call of the unit of work", and harness/policy/interface.py makes it checkable, with admit running decide before the work callable and ordering returning decisions taken alongside decisions whose record precedes that dispatch first metered call.
falsifier: A dispatch whose policy-decided record does not precede its first metered call, or a denied dispatch with a non-zero spend delta. Run: python3 harness/policy/conformance.py over both bindings and read decided_before_first_metered_call and spend_delta_micros.
note: The declaration is a contract and a counter, not an intention: the meter and the decision journal draw sequence numbers from one counter, so before is a comparison of two integers rather than a claim about the code path.

evidence: Worked case I ran, with the refusal. python3 harness/idempotency/call.py: submit returned fresh, replay of the same key and payload returned duplicate with the same result_ref, ten concurrent submissions of one key returned fresh=1 duplicate=9, and reusing that key under a different payload was refused with urn:agentic:problem:idempotency-conflict, status 409, retryable false, as harness/idempotency/README.md describes it, "refused as the typed `idempotency-conflict`, 409". Per entry point: bash examples/end-to-end/test.sh replays an entry and reports "zero new records, exit code 0" behaviour, measured as replay recognised with the ledger still at 56 records, and bash harness/linked/test.sh reports replays that were no-ops (4), one per door, alongside 4 typed refusals.
falsifier: A second effect for a replayed key, a replay that appends a record, or a reused key under a different payload that is accepted. Run: the three commands above, and bash harness/idempotency/test.sh, whose breakage removes the lease acquisition and leaves the key on the wire.
note: The breakage measured here: with the lease removed, every one of 20 concurrent copies executed and only the race case failed, 7/8, so the check discriminates. The dry-run bindings are measured; the on-disk live ledger path is claimed in harness/idempotency/provenance.json.
